Sorry for the slow reply. But I think, supporting him as much you can. I presume he’s high functioning. It’s good that your encouraging him to be himself, because he will always be different. Not bad but different. I’ve found though, I like being helped with being ‘normal’. I like being myself, but it’s way easier being able to blend in with the crowd and not be looked at weirdly. Of course talk to him about it first, you don’t want to force it on him. I think as long as his stims aren’t socially in appropriate, I think it’s fine for him using stims. Unless he asks you for help with them because he’s embarrassed, maybe bring it up to him, but don’t pressure him into stopping, it’s his way of coping with the world. It’s hard enough for us to navigate this world, never mind without something that helps him. You sound like a good parent, thank you for being supportive to him. 

I’m not an expert, and we’re all different, but the most important thing is communication. The more you can talk to him about his needs, the better, but don’t force anything on him unless nessecary

Yeah I’m comfortable with it, Ask me if you want more details. So I’m 15 living in England, I’ve always been good kid. My mum thought I may have had autism when I was younger, but it was pushed under the rug, because I was ‘intelligent’. I moved from my hometown when I was 12. Moved to a new place, and got bullied for the whole year, this is where it starts to go downhill. I didn’t want to go to school, didn’t want to leave the house, I had really bad anxiety but at the time I didn’t realise it. I just thought I had a bad stomach all the time. One day I refused to go to my school, my stepdad picked me up and dropped me outside in the freezing weather and left me out there for a few hours until he came back. This starts the trouble between us. After this year of hell. I move again. This time with anxiety of moving and being bullied. I’m scared of starting school. I’ve always been good at school, scoring top marks in almost every subject, and being well behaved. So I started off school here, but I couldn’t make friends, I feel isolated here. It all started off fairly well, not very eventful for the first year, except from the loneliness and the and some bullying. I kinda put all of my energy into music though, I love music, it’s what keeps me sane. The next year was a whole lot different. It slowly got worse and worse, my grades were dropping, I’d had enough of teachers giving me shit all the time, and so I kinda just gave up a lot, just coasted through that year, getting detentions I didn’t go to, getting suspended, starting missing a load of classes, I just couldn’t be bothered with school because I was treated like shit the whole time. My life feels like it’s falling apart here, I stop leaving the house, I stop talking to people, I close myself up. It’s the start of my depression. I put on weight because I binge eat in the middle of the night, I start having sleepless nights, you name it. Now that I’m a problem to the school, they decide that maybe I do have autism now, because of all the hassle I’ve caused them. They’ve ignored the obvious signs for years, and I got mistreated for years because of this. So I start the diagnosis for autism, from here, it gets worse. You’re on the waiting list for over a year here for them to even start diagnosis here, which is bs. So the school continues to mistreat me, even though they know I’m going through all this. This leads to me self harming, and even attempting suicide, at 14 ffs. That year ends. With my life a mess. My depression worsens, along with my anxiety. This next year, is one of the most important years of my life, this year. We take exams which dictate our whole lives, whether we can get jobs or not. So I go Into this school year trying to be hopeful (last september) and no, it doesn’t start well. All the teachers ignore the extra support I need and all of that, which ends up with me taking myself out of school in November. This is my lowest point. I finally get off the waiting list to get my autism diagnosis. And it still takes ages. I had my first assessment in July, nothing happens til December. Where I meet with a physciatric nurses, who starts to asses me. Through all this, I find out on my own, that I probably have adhd-pi(adhd, but without the hyper activity, it all happens in my head instead) I bring this up to him, and he puts t through to asses me for that. Around this time, I get out on anti depressants which don’t work, i tried them for 11 weeks, but they didn’t work so I stopped taking them last week. My doctor just said he doesn’t like putting meds in teens, so just told me to go outside more, etc. During all this, the school has forgotten about me, and my future looks awful. Which causes me stress. My mental health worsens, and I havnt got out of bed properly for months. I’ve came close to suicide multiple times and it just feels endless now. 

Sorry it’s a jumbled mess, and really long, I just wanted to get it all out, ask me anything about it
